Samsung Begins Full Scale Advance Development of "1.4 Nanometer" Process

Samsung Electronics is restarting its push toward commercializing the 1.4nm foundry process (SF1.4). The 1.4nm process, which was originally targeted for mass production in 2027, has had its schedule adjusted and development is now proceeding with a mass production target of 2029.

It is understood that Samsung has recently asked domestic and overseas partners to begin advance development of equipment for the process. The equipment is set to be brought into NRD-K, Samsung Electronics' next generation semiconductor research and development (R&D) hub.

According to industry sources on the 25th, Samsung Electronics recently shared its 1.4nm process plans with major semiconductor equipment makers such as Applied Materials (Applied) and Lam Research. Along with this, it is reported to have requested advance development of equipment.

Applied and Lam Research are key equipment partners for Samsung Electronics. Equipment from these companies is widely applied across both foundry and memory processes.

These companies develop equipment in cooperation with chipmakers such as Samsung Electronics starting from the process development stage. The structure is one in which the required equipment specifications are presented and the equipment is then designed and developed to match them.

The 1.4nm process that Samsung Electronics is preparing to commercialize was a technology originally targeted for mass production next year. However, the company adjusted the 1.4nm mass production schedule to 2029 in order to concentrate its capabilities on securing the competitiveness of the 2nm (SF2) and the 2nm derivative process (SF2P).

The decision was aimed at building internal strength by focusing on yield stabilization and optimization of existing processes rather than forcing the leading edge process ahead prematurely.

The strategy appears to have paid off. Samsung Electronics stabilized the yield of its 2nm process and went on to succeed in winning orders for the production volume of Tesla's next generation artificial intelligence (AI) chip.

Having delivered results on the 2nm process, the company now appears to be moving into preparation for its next generation process. The next generation equipment developed by partners will be brought into NRD-K and used for 1.4nm process development.

ASML's next generation lithography equipment, the high NA extreme ultraviolet (EUV) tool, has already been brought into NRD-K. High NA EUV is understood to be applied to some layers starting from the 1.4nm process.

Domestic partners are also closely watching the trends in Samsung Electronics' next generation process development. As process difficulty continues to rise, sufficient development time is needed to develop equipment that matches the process specifications required by the customer.

As Samsung Electronics again picks up the pace on 1.4nm process development, attention is focused on whether it can narrow the technology gap with competitors such as TSMC. TSMC is targeting commercialization of its 1.4nm process in 2028. Intel is proceeding with development aimed at mass production next year.

In addition, Samsung Electronics is understood to have also requested equipment orders for the development of its next generation V12 NAND. V12 NAND is expected to enter full scale mass production around 2030. As it applies a structure that stacks multiple wafers, its storage capacity and performance are significantly improved compared with existing NAND.

A senior official at a global semiconductor equipment company explained that equipment makers discuss with chipmakers from the early stages when they develop a next generation process, and that there are many cases where equipment is developed to match the process requirements.
